title: After the Ballots, Markets Look Ahead | Dimensional
gist: Wes Crill (Dimensional) argues stocks rise over the long run regardless of party, but elections are price discovery events: after the 2026 US midterms the Russell 3000 fell ~2.8% over Nov 4-5 with sectors ranging from -8.07% (tech) to +2.84% (communication services). Historically, election-month sector winners and losers converge back to market returns afterward.

insights.claim: Over the long term, US stocks have generally kept rising regardless of which political party held office, so election outcomes are not a reliable basis for long-run market timing.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill
insights.so_what: Avoid repositioning a long-term equity allocation around which party wins.
insights.quote: stocks have generally continued their ascent regardless of which political party was in office

insights.claim: Markets do not ignore politics: elections act as a price discovery event in which stocks of companies expected to benefit from the result jump and those perceived as losers fall.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill
insights.so_what: Expect sharp cross-sectional repricing right after elections rather than broad directional moves.
insights.quote: elections are a price discovery opportunity for market participants
insights.locator: That doesn’t mean markets ignore politics

insights.claim: Over November 4-5, 2026, right after the US midterm elections, the Russell 3000 Index fell about 2.8% while sector returns ranged from -8.07% for technology to +2.84% for communication services.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill
insights.so_what: Post-midterm dispersion was wide: tech was hit hardest, communication services held up.
insights.locator: The days following the recent US midterm elections

insights.claim: The post-midterm sell-off in technology reversed 2026 year-to-date leadership: through Election Day, technology stocks had returned 23.1% versus 11.6% for the Russell 3000.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill
insights.so_what: Crowded YTD winners can be the most exposed to repricing on a surprise political outcome.
insights.locator: This was quite a change from the 2026 results

insights.claim: The wide sector dispersion after the 2026 US midterms likely reflects the market resetting expectations for certain businesses after results many viewed as surprising.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill
insights.so_what: Treat the post-election moves as expectation resets priced in quickly, not as an ongoing trend to chase.
insights.locator: The dispersion among sectors could be evidence

insights.claim: Sectors with the largest outperformance or underperformance versus the market during election months tend to perform in line with the broader market afterward, so election-night winners do not reliably keep winning.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill
insights.so_what: Don't extrapolate election-month sector moves; post-election mean-convergence argues against chasing or panic-selling.
insights.quote: election night winners don’t always continue to win
insights.locator: Of course, it’s important for investors to remember

source_meta.author: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
